correctness.rationale: On a simple cycle each zero has one zero neighbor by restraint and must have a 3 as its other neighbor. Hence all zeros occur in pairs, and each intervening positive run begins and ends at 3. Relative to length including the preceding zero pair, a singleton run 3 has excess 0, and any longer run costs at least 2 extra. Equality in the latter bound forces all interior labels to be 1; precisely 33, 313 and 3113 qualify. At optimum the total excess is zero for 3|n and two otherwise; reducing the length of the unique longer run modulo three selects 33 or 313. With no zeros, the set of 2/3 vertices dominates and adds at least ceil(n/3) above n. Only n=4,5 can tie in the nonzero residues: one 3 cannot dominate, whereas two 2's work at any pair on C4 (six choices) and exactly at the five nonadjacent pairs on C5. The periodic word has period three; the single 33 or 1 marker makes the defect words full period. Reversal gives a rotation, and the no-zero extra orbits are identified by pair distance. Replacing coefficients 3j by 3 for j>=2 in the baseline sum of n t^n gives the stated subtraction; the two small exceptions give +6t^4+5t^5. Independent exhaustive comparison of entire winner sets at n=3..8 passed using /workspace/review_checks.py (cycles); this corroborates but is not the all-orders proof. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; its transfer recurrence counts labeled cyclic words through a fixed index, not orbits.
